The permanganate ion ($\text{MnO}_4^-$) contains manganese in the +7 oxidation state. The electronic configuration of $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^0$.

Ligand-field analysis, and the determination of parameters such as the splitting parameter $Dq$ and the Racah parameters $B$ and $C$, relies on the analysis of $d$-$d$ electronic transitions. Since $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ has no electrons in its $d$-orbitals ($d^0$), $d$-$d$ transitions are impossible. 

The intense absorption bands observed at 17,570 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, 31,560 $\text{cm}^{-1}$, and 38,320 $\text{cm}^{-1}$ (with high molar extinction coefficients $\epsilon > 1,000 \text{ M}^{-1} \text{cm}^{-1}$) are characteristic of ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) transitions, specifically from the oxygen $2p$ orbitals to the empty manganese $3d$ orbitals. These transitions are not governed by the ligand-field splitting of $d$-electrons or interelectronic repulsion within the $d$-shell.

Consequently, $Dq$ and $B$ cannot be determined for this complex using the provided data.
